archetype.name: Play-In Team (shorthanded)
archetype.definition: A roster whose healthy level, judged by recent seasons, sits around the play-in line, now playing well below it because its best creator and two rotation guards have been missing or limited.

report.headline: A 2-7 start that is earned, but mostly by who isn't playing
report.take:
Orlando's 2-7 record is not bad luck. The W vs Pt Diff is exactly 0, the margin implies 2 wins, and the Net Rtg of -9.3 ranks 25th. The ratings are poor on both ends: the 107.9 ORtg is 27th and the 117.2 DRtg is 26th. A team built on defense has lost that identity. This club ranked 2nd in defense in both 2023-24 and 2024-25 and 11th last year. Over a full season it would project to 18 wins, but this nine-game sample is badly distorted by the roster.

Paolo Banchero has played two games. In those he posted a 77 TS% and a 7.2 BPM, and he is now listed Out. Jalen Suggs has played three games and is also Out. Anthony Black, the best-graded player here (10th of 83 point guards), has appeared in only six, and Desmond Bane is day-to-day. Without them, Franz Wagner carries a 28.9 USG % on 51.9 TS%, and Jase Richardson has soaked up big backcourt minutes at a 38.9 TS%. That explains the backcourt grade of D, and it explains why November has looked worse than October: scoring fell from 109.8 a game to 103.5 and the team lost all four games.

The structure underneath is better than the results. Opponents take only 26% of their shots at the rim, 5th-fewest in the league. The defensive glass ranks 9th. Wendell Carter Jr. is scoring at a 73 TS% with a +16.9 On-Off. The holes are turnovers, with a TOV % of 15.7 that ranks 27th, and opponents hitting 37.8% from three, 25th. Some of that three-point damage is the kind of shooting that cools off over a larger sample. The defense will not get back to its 2024-25 level without healthy guards, but it should not stay 26th either.

The 2-7 hole is real, and the division is already led by Atlanta at 7-4. The coming week, though, is the softest stretch the schedule is likely to offer. If Orlando cannot bank wins against three 1-9 teams, the slow start stops being about injuries.

strengths.title: Keeping opponents away from the rim
strengths.body: Opponents take only 26% of their shots within four feet, 5th-lowest in the league and well under the league's 29.8. That shot profile has been part of this team for years: the Opp Rim Rate has stayed in the high 20s to low 30s through recent seasons. It holds up even with the guards missing, so it should last.

strengths.title: Carter Jr. as the efficient anchor
strengths.body: Carter is shooting a 73 TS% on a low 15.3 USG %, and the team is far better with him on the floor. That fits the frontcourt's B- grade, the best group on the roster. His efficiency will drift down, but his role as a finisher and rebounder (86 boards) is stable.

strengths.title: Black has been the best guard
strengths.body: Anthony Black has a 3.4 BPM, a 59.9 TS% and an 11.2 On-Off, and ranks 10th on the point guard tab. He has played only six games, so the sample is small. Still, he is the one guard on the roster producing clearly positive numbers, and more of his minutes would directly patch the D backcourt.

concerns.title: Banchero's absence breaks the offense
concerns.body: In two games Banchero posted a 77 TS% and a 7.2 BPM. Without him, Wagner's usage climbs to 28.9% at a 51.9 TS%, and the offense ranks 27th. The fix is health rather than scheme, so this lasts exactly as long as he is out.

concerns.title: Turnovers on a thin backcourt
concerns.body: The 15.7 TOV % ranks 27th, a big jump from the 12.4 of last season. The cause is that inexperienced guards are doing the ball-handling: Richardson, for example, is at a 38.9 TS%. It should ease when Suggs and Black are healthy, but for now it costs possessions the offense cannot spare.

concerns.title: A defense far below its standard
concerns.body: The DRtg of 117.2 ranks 26th, against a defense that ranked 2nd two seasons running. Two things are driving it. Opponents are making 37.8% of their threes (25th), which is partly noise over nine games. Power forwards are also scoring freely: they account for 24.8% of points against, well above the league's share, which points to the hole Banchero left.

trend.note: A 2-3 October gave way to an 0-4 November as scoring dropped. The last five games did tighten the defense slightly, with 2.62 fewer points allowed a game than the season average.

weekAhead.headline: Three 1-9 teams, then Boston: the week to climb out
weekAhead.body:
Three of the four games are against Sacramento, Utah and Milwaukee, all 1-9 and all ranked 27th or lower on the site. Two of those are road games on consecutive nights, Sacramento and then Utah. Sacramento and Milwaukee own two of the league's worst defenses. Utah is weak in a different way: its 104.4 ORtg ranks 29th, worse than Orlando's offense.

The week closes at Boston, which ranks 1st in Net Rtg at 11.2 and 6th in defense. Anything better than one loss in the first three games would be a real step. Splitting them would confirm that the problem runs deeper than the schedule.

keyMatchups.title: Carter against Sacramento's soft rim
keyMatchups.body: Sacramento allows a 75% finish at the rim, last in the league, and centers score 24.1 a game against it. That suits Carter's high-efficiency interior role. It is the clearest path to easy points for a struggling offense.

keyMatchups.title: Utah's leaky point-guard defense
keyMatchups.body: Utah gives up 33.5 points a game to point guards, among the most in the league. It is stingy against small forwards, ranking 3rd in points allowed to them, which squeezes Wagner. Expect the offense to run through whichever of Black and the healthy guards are available, rather than through the wings.

keyMatchups.title: Milwaukee won't punish turnovers
keyMatchups.body: Milwaukee forces the fewest turnovers in the league, which eases Orlando's biggest leak. Its defense also gives up big lines to centers, well above their usual output. This home game is the best chance of the week for a clean offensive night.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Bane and Black are both available for the back-to-back in Sacramento and Utah. Healthy guards are the difference between a sweep and another split.

restOfSeason.body:
The current pace of 18 wins is the floor of a depleted roster, not a forecast. The structural pieces are still in place: rim deterrence, defensive rebounding and Carter's efficiency. The disasters are tied to absences, namely the turnovers, Wagner's overload and the power-forward defense, and opponents' three-point shooting should come back toward the league norm. With Banchero and the guards back, a team that won 41 to 47 games in each of the last three seasons should play near .500 the rest of the way. That climbs out of the hole toward the high 30s, but probably not all the way.

The risk is the calendar. The 2-7 start already trails Atlanta, and if Banchero's absence runs long, a play-in spot becomes the ceiling rather than the floor. If he returns soon and the defense recovers toward last year's 11th, Orlando can still finish in the 30s and contend for the play-in.
swingFactors: Whether the defense returns toward its top-10 level

confidence.note: Nine games, a heavily injured roster and on-off numbers in tiny samples make the current line noisy, but the multi-season history gives a firm baseline.
